title: Taranga 4. Srinivasa's Journey to Vrindavana
html:
Srinivasa in Navadvipa: Vamshivadana, Vishnupriya, Vishnupriya's dream, her renunciation, the mercy of the Lord's associates; Shantipura — the vision of Advaita and Sita's blessing; Khardaha — Jahnava and Virachandra; Khanakul — Abhirama and his whip; farewell to Narahari and to his mother; the journey to Vrindavana; news of the Gosvamis' departure; meeting with Jiva, initiation by Gopala Bhatta; Narottama

1Glory to the Moon of Navadvipa, the son of Shachi,
the Lord of the helpless, the life of the devotees!

2Glory to Nityananda, the son of Padmavati,
the Lord who purifies the world, supremely merciful!

3Glory, glory to Gadadhara, the son of Madhava!
Glory, glory to Srivasa and the other devotees of the Lord!

4Glory, glory to the listeners, abodes of virtue!
Listen kindly to what I shall now relate.

5At the edge of Navadvipa, Srinivasa, deeply stirred,
weeps as he gazes towards Navadvipa.

6He sat for a while beneath a tree
and with great effort regained his composure.

7Wondrous are Gauranga's pastimes in Navadvipa;
thinking of them, he again lost his composure.

8As he enters Navadvipa he sees a marvel:
the Lord's manifest pastimes amid the company of devotees.

9Singing the supremely wondrous virtues of Gauranga,
the women of Navadvipa run to and fro.

10Sankirtana, auspicious for the world, is in every house;
a river of bliss flows through the town of Nadia.

11Seeing this, Srinivasa forgot himself;
who could tell how his joy grew?

12He gazed so for a while, and then he sees
that all are constantly drowning in an ocean of grief.

13Astonished, Srinivasa goes on
and asks everyone where the Lord's house is.

14No one can say anything — they are bathed in tears;
Srinivasa walks along the road in distress.

15"Ha, ha, Gaura, Gadadhara, Lord of my life!"
he cries aloud, raising both arms.

16"Ha, ha, Prabhu Nityananda, Advaita, merciful ones!"
Saying this, he lost all composure.

17He weeps so that stones would split.
Then suddenly a man came up.

18Amazed at the sight of this extraordinary youth,
he showed him the way to the Lord's house.

19Coming near the house, he looks all around
and stands in one place like a wooden doll.

20Sri Vamshivadana,1 seeing him, without any introduction
thought to himself, "This must be Srinivasa."

21Coming near, he asked who he was;
Srinivasa told him everything from beginning to end.

22Sri Vamshivadana embraced him
and bathed Srinivasa in his own tears.

23Srinivasa, falling to the ground, wishes to bow down,
but Sri Thakura Vamshi will not release him from his embrace.

24To inform Sri Ishvari, Mother Vishnupriya,2
Sri Vamshivadana went [to her] with care.

25Meanwhile Vishnupriya says to her dear maidservant,
"I have had a dream; I will tell you what is in my heart.

26The world-enchanting Lord, the master of my life,
came before me — how sweet His gait!

27The splendour of His beauty destroys the pride of Kama —
what a poor comparison is a flash of lightning!

28How beautifully His whole body is anointed with sandal —
as if carefully smeared with the ground autumn moon.

29He is adorned with ornaments, clad in [fine] garments;
He captivates even the modesty of young maidens, and there is no fear in the heart.

30Ah, what lovely, glossy, curling hair!
What fragrance — who would not lose himself in it?

31His two long eyes surpass lotus petals;
seeing His glance, no one can stay composed.

32Arms reaching to the knees, an enchanting bearing;
how broad His chest, which maddens the world!

33On that moonlike face is a gentle smile;
I know not what nectar it showers in torrents!

34With what tenderness He seated me on a seat
and softly speaks sweet words to me:

35'There is a brahmana youth named Srinivasa;
there is no counting the sorrows he has suffered.

36Today he will come to see you;
knowing him as your own, show him mercy.'

37Saying much in this way and showing such joy,
He disappeared, and I awoke in sorrow.

38I understood that he is very dear to the Lord of my life,
and I feel that he will soon come."

39Just then Sri Vamshivadana announced,
"Srinivasa has come here from Nilachala."

40Hearing this, Ishvari wished to see him,
and Srinivasa went before Ishvari.

41Streams of love flow incessantly from his eyes;
rolling on the ground, he bows down again and again.

42Ishvari, hearing that Srinivasa was bowing,
stood concealed, remembering Gauranga.3

43Her heart burns in the forest fire of separation from the Lord,
and yet, seeing Srinivasa, she feels joy.

44Speaking sweet words with motherly affection and mercy,
she placed her feet on Srinivasa's head.

45Ordering that he be served mahaprasada,
she became motionless, her heart drowning in tears.

46Someone gave Srinivasa prasada in a secluded place;
he honoured the prasada, bathed in tears.

47Every day Srinivasa has [her] darshan;
Ishvari's way of life cannot be described.

48In separation from the Lord, sleep has left her eyes;
if she sleeps at all, it is on the bare ground.

49Her body, which surpassed gold, has grown very dark;
she is wasted like the moon on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight.

50She keeps count of the names of Hari with grains of rice;
that rice she cooks and offers to the Lord.4

51Only a tiny portion of it does she eat;
no one knows how she keeps alive.

52How she gave Srinivasa darshan day after day,
and what state he was in — who can describe it?

53Then everyone understood
that she kept this body for the sake of mercy to Srinivasa.

54All praise Srinivasa's good fortune:
there is none so worthy of mercy as Srinivasa.

55What mercy Mother Shachi showed Srinivasa, appearing as if in a dream —
where shall I find the power to describe it?

56Through Navadvipa the word spread:
"Srinivasa, the vessel of Gaura's love, has come."

57Sri Murari, Srivasa Pandita, Damodara,
Sanjaya, Vijaya, Shuklambara Brahmachari,

58Dasa Gadadhara and the other dear ones of the Lord —
all showed mercy to Srinivasa.

59Although in separation from the Lord all were nearly dead,
yet by the Lord's will they felt joy.

60For the sake of mercy to Srinivasa —
for this [the Lord] kept His associates manifest.

61Srivasa's wife and the other chaste ladies —
their motherly affection for Srinivasa cannot be written.

62Keeping Srinivasa with them for some days,
all told him to go quickly to Vrindavana.

63Taking leave of everyone, his heart aching,
he goes to Shantipura, to the house of Prabhu Advaita.

64As he entered Shantipura, he was overcome with grief;
Prabhu Sri Advaita appeared to him and consoled him.5

65Srinivasa is not at peace and thinks to himself,
"What a wonder I saw! It must be an illusion."

66As he pondered thus, the command came again,
and his mind's doubt was dispelled; his joy was boundless.

67Bathed in tears, thinking of that form,
he quickly came to the Prabhu's abode.

68Hearing that Srinivasa had come,
everyone grew eager to see him.

69In separation from the Lord all were distraught at heart,
and everyone's body had grown weak.

70In Mother Sita's body life barely remained;
she called Srinivasa into the inner apartments.

71Srinivasa went and bowed to her feet;
in her mercy she placed her feet on his head.

72Tears stream incessantly from both her eyes;
in a faltering voice she says to Srinivasa:

73"O my son Srinivasa, I have been waiting for you;
it is good that you have come — I am happy to see you.

74Live long on the earth:
through you good will come to living beings.

75You will distribute this rare prema-bhakti
and spread the scriptures of bhakti, the whole treasure of the devotees.

76Some will join you after a while,
and with them you will find steadiness amid all these sorrows.

77You will have many followers;
you will float ceaselessly in the joy of sankirtana.

78You must go quickly to Vrindavana:
there you will become a disciple, and your desire will be fulfilled."

79Saying much, she entrusted him to Madana-gopala6
and introduced him to her sons and servants.

80Her motherly affection for Srinivasa I cannot describe;
instructing him in many ways, she gave him leave.

81Bowing to everyone, Srinivasa Mahashaya
went to Khardaha, to the abode of Prabhu Nityananda.

82Seeing Srinivasa, Sri Parameshvari Dasa,7
though in great sorrow, felt joy.

83He was sure in his mind that this was Srinivasa,
and coming near, he learned who he was.

84Through the village of Khardaha the news spread:
"Srinivasa of Chakhandi has come here."

85All, eager to see Srinivasa,
went to where Srinivasa was.

86Meanwhile Sri Parameshvari Dasa
quickly took Srinivasa to the Prabhu's house.

87Srinivasa, ever bathed in tears,
bowed down and fell at the feet of Ishvari.

88Sri Vasu[dha] and Jahnava, together with Virabhadra,8
were very pleased to see Srinivasa.

89Although the terrible grief was unbearable,
still joy arose in everyone's heart.

90He stayed there four or five days;
no one could bear to part with Srinivasa.

91Suryadasa, Gauridasa, Pandita Mahesha —
many devotees there showed him boundless mercy.

92Sri Jahnava, the Prabhu [Virabhadra] and the others, their hearts aching,
ordered him to go to Vrindavana.

93Sri Vasu and Jahnavi again say with loving feeling,
"Go quickly to the house of Abhirama Gopala."

94Srinivasa bowed down and took leave;
he is ceaselessly bathed in streams from both eyes.

95Thinking of Nityananda's qualities, he was greatly agitated;
by His will he saw many mysteries.

96Srinivasa floated in that ocean of bliss;
he set out to go to Abhirama.

97With great eagerness he walks along the road;
on the way to Virloka a companion joined him —9

98an old brahmana whose home was in Khanakula.10
With a pleased heart he asks Srinivasa,

99"What is your name, son, and where are you going?"
Srinivasa bowed to him and told him.

100Hearing this, the brahmana, overcome with love, says,
"I heard about you in Khardaha.

101Come, my son Srinivasa, let me embrace you!"
So saying, he took him in his arms and was bathed in tears.

102"Sri Thakura Abhirama is an abode of virtues;
he will show you great mercy.

103The power of Abhirama Gosvami is formidable:
seeing him, even invincible unbelievers tremble.

104He is ever mad with absorption in Nityananda;
his charming mercy is known throughout the world.

105O Srinivasa, how much shall I tell you?
He descended in a brahmana's house to deliver living beings.

106He is learned in all the shastras, supremely charming,
an incomparable master of dance, song and music.

107By the will of Prabhu Nityananda-Balarama
he married, [taking a wife] from the house of a learned brahmana.

108Sri Abhirama's wife is named Sri Malini;
I cannot tell all her glory.

109O Srinivasa, Sri Thakura Abhirama
is, in Krishna's pastimes, the famous Shridama.11

110Now he has revealed that former nature:
to a certain servant he appeared in the form of Shridama.

111Sri Thakura Abhirama is the embodiment of prema;
all worship him — who does not proclaim his fame?

112Thus [it is said] in a verse of his disciple Sri Vedagarbha Acharya:
"I worship the venerable Abhirama, formerly called Shridama,
the embodiment of love, the crest-jewel of brahmanas, the husband of Sri Malini."

113O Srinivasa, how wondrous is his conduct!
He grew eager to serve the Deity.

114Gopinatha appeared to him as if in a dream,
said, 'Here I abide,' and showed him the place.

115Digging at that place, Abhirama
found the incomparable Deity of Gopinatha.

116The news spread everywhere, and all the people come running;
the moment they have darshan they forget grief and sorrow.

117The divine water of the pond where Gopinatha appeared —
bathing in it and drinking it, all became overwhelmed with bliss.

118It became famous as Rama-kunda;
there is no end to the people who come and go.

119Malini and Sri Abhirama with their people
joyfully serve Sri Gopinatha.

120From time to time Prabhu Nityananda with His associates
would come to the house of His dear Abhirama.

121One day Abhirama, intoxicated with the bliss of love,
was dancing — that pose of his is incomparable.

122Absorbed in sakhya-rasa, he wants to play the flute;
he searches here and there but cannot find his flute.

123A log that even a hundred men could not move
he took in his hand as a flute.

124Seeing this, all were greatly astonished;
from time to time he has such superhuman pastimes.

125Now that Nityananda-Balarama has disappeared,
he constantly sighs deeply and speaks to no one.

126Only the fortunate understand this inscrutable conduct;
you will see it yourself, son — be careful."

127Saying this, the brahmana, full of affection,
showed him Sri Abhirama's house.

128Srinivasa bowed to the brahmana's feet
and remembered Nityananda-chandra.

129Holding in his heart the strength of Ishvari's command,
he went and reached Sri Abhirama's house.

130Bowing down, he stayed at the outer gate;
through Virloka the news of Srinivasa's arrival spread.

131Thakura Abhirama, in separation from Sri Prabhu,
is always absorbed in love and says nothing to anyone.

132Knowing that Srinivasa had come, he smiles gently
and resolves in his mind, "I shall test him."

133He gave him ten kards of cowries for his keep;12
with them [Srinivasa] bought what was needed.

134Then he went to the bank of the Darukeshvara river,13
cooked, and offered the food to Krishna.

135At that moment the Thakura sent four men;
seeing them, Srinivasa rejoiced at heart.

136Bowing to them, he fed the four
and himself honoured that mahaprasada.

137Srinivasa's conduct gladdened everyone's heart;
they tell the Thakura, "We have come back well fed."

138All these tests were to teach others;
he had Srinivasa brought before him.

139With his whip named Jayamangala
he touched Srinivasa's body three times.14

140Joyfully touching him with that whip,
he laughs aloud, saying something to Srinivasa.

141When in loving rapture he was about to touch him with the whip again,
Sri Malini-devi came and held his hand.

142Malini says, "Restrain yourself, Gosani:
there is no limit to the mercy you have shown.

143Srinivasa is only a boy; he will not be able to stay steady;
if he goes mad with love, how will he accomplish his task?"

144So speaking together with pleased hearts,
the two place their hands on Srinivasa's head.

145Srinivasa fell at the feet of both;
raising him up, they bathed him in tears.

146All the affection the two showed Srinivasa —
have I the power to tell it?

147Entrusting him to the feet of Radha-Gopinatha,
the two ordered him to go to Vrindavana.

148All the residents of Sri Krishnanagara and Khanakula,
on seeing Srinivasa, felt their affection ever increase.

149Taking leave of all the Vaishnavas,
he came again to Shrikhanda, his heart in distress.

150Sri Thakura Narahari and Sri Raghunandana,
seeing Srinivasa, embraced him tightly.

151They gently asked him about everything,
and Srinivasa told them, bathed in tears.

152Thakura Sri Narahari and Sri Raghunandana
gave him permission to go to Vrindavana.

153The Thakura again took Srinivasa in his arms;
unable to let him go, he is bathed in tears.

154He told him everything about the road;
at the moment of parting his heart was rent.

155Bowing to both Sri Thakura Narahari and Sri Raghunandana,
he set out at an auspicious moment.

156How he went along the road cannot be described;
reaching Yajigrama, he saw his mother.

157Telling her everything,
he asks her leave to go quickly to Vrindavana.

158Hearing this, his mother's heart was troubled,
but she could not forbid Srinivasa.

159For five or seven days she lovingly kept her son with her;
Srinivasa, reassuring her, took his leave.

160Bowing again and again at his mother's feet,
he set off, after meeting all the villagers.

161On the second day of the bright fortnight of Agrahayana he left home15
and stopped a short way off, by someone's arrangement.

162At Agradvipa and other villages, in the houses of devotees,
taking leave everywhere, he came to Kantaka-nagara.16

163Where Mahaprabhu accepted sannyasa,
there in loving rapture he wept much.

164Going quickly from there to Maudeshvara,17
he was gladdened at heart by the sight of Shiva.

165There the people told Srinivasa
how the Lord had delivered [them] from the fear of snakes.

166Seeing the place of Kundali-damana, Srinivasa
heaves deep sighs, saying, "Prabhu Nityananda!"18

167The wise Srinivasa, who attracts every heart,
went to Ekachakra, where the house of Hadai Ojha is.19

168Entering it, he felt it to be Shvetadvipa;
he gazed his fill at Nityananda's birthplace.

169Seeing all the places where Prabhu Nityananda
had enacted the pastimes of Rama, he was overwhelmed.

170Raising his arms, he sings Nityananda's virtues,
ceaselessly floating in the streams from both his eyes.

171Grey with dust, he rolls on the ground;
by the Lord's will sleep came to his aid.

172As if in a dream he directly sees a great festivity:
Nityananda sporting with His companions.

173Beholding [Nityananda's] beauty with His associates,
his bliss increased, and his eyes and mind were soothed.

174On waking he felt boundless grief;
the Prabhu had ordered him to go to Vrindavana.

175Bowing to the village of Ekachakra,
Srinivasa set off, remembering Nityananda's feet.

176Whatever village Srinivasa passes through,
all its inhabitants run to see him.

177All try in many ways to feed him something;
Srinivasa does whatever makes them all happy.

178After some days he arrived at Gaya-kshetra;
he sees the lotus feet of Vishnu, absorbed in love.

179There Mahaprabhu met Ishvara Puri;20
remembering all this, his eyes stream constantly.

180Whoever sees Srinivasa, woman or man,
loses all composure and is ever bathed in tears.

181How wondrous his early youth, full of supreme bliss!
Seeing him once, one cannot leave his company.

182Thus attracting every heart,
he went to Kashi and saw Chandrashekhara's house.

183There a disciple of Chandrashekhara, a great soul,
seeing Srinivasa, rejoiced at heart.21

184Learning who he was, he lost his composure in love;
taking Srinivasa in his arms, he began to weep.

185Showing him where the Lord had stayed,
he lovingly kept him for two or four days.

186With all the Lord's followers who were in Kashi
he met there.

187Taking leave, he went on very quickly;
seeing Ayodhya and Prayaga, he was absorbed in love.

188From there Srinivasa went towards Vraja;
many longings arise in his heart.

189Holding the lotus feet of Rupa and Sanatana in his heart,
he hastily entered the city of Mathura.

190Where Krishna rested after killing Kamsa —
Sri Vishrama-ghata — there he arrived.22

191Along that road came two or four brahmanas,
speaking of Sri Vrindavana.

192One says, "Why so much misfortune?
What joy is left to taste in this wretched life?

193Who can understand anything of the Supreme Lord's will?
One by one this place has been emptied of its jewels.

194At Nilachala Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the Lord of all,
became invisible to everyone's eyes.

195Hearing that unbearable news,
Kashishvara Gosvami disappeared.

196Raghunatha Bhatta, the reciter of the Bhagavata —
in separation from the Lord he too disappeared.

197Some days ago Sri Gosani Sanatana
disappeared from our eyes.

198And now Sri Rupa Gosani has left the manifest world;
we have come from seeing it — our grief knows no bounds.

199Sri Gopala Bhatta, Raghunatha and all the others
are ceaselessly burning in the flames of the fire of separation.

200I have understood here that our fortune is bad;
otherwise would we see sorrow in the midst of such happiness?"23

201As they went along lamenting much in this way,
Srinivasa anxiously asked them.

202Weeping, that man told Srinivasa
the account of the disappearance of Sanatana and Rupa.

203Hearing it, Srinivasa was bathed in tears
and fell unconscious on the ground.

204"Alas, alas, what have I heard!" he cries, rising again;
grey with dust, he rolls on the earth again.

205Again he says, "Ha, ha, Prabhu Rupa and Sanatana!
Why have you dealt so with this lowly one?

206I did not see your holy feet; my hope was not fulfilled!"
Saying this, Srinivasa tears his breast with his nails.

207Seeing this, the brahmana of Mathura seized his hand
and took great pains to save his life.

208All the residents of Mathura were astonished;
they consoled him much, but he would not consent [to live].

209Bowing to the brahmana of Mathura,
Srinivasa turned back again towards the east.

210He reflects, "The masters in Gauda and in the Kshetra
all told me, 'Go quickly to Vrindavana.'

211This is why they gave that order, and I did not understand;
unfortunate as I am, I could not come quickly.

212Cruel fate has brought so much misfortune,
and still life remains in this sinful body."

213As he pondered thus, tears streamed from both eyes;
he falls silent, then again cries out in anguish:

214"O Sanatana, Rupa, oceans of virtue,
Raghunatha Bhatta, Sri Pandita Kashishvara!

215I heard that you are supremely merciful —
why have you become merciless to one as wretched as I?"

216Saying much like this, he wishes to give up his life;
he falls, flinging himself down, not knowing where he is.

217Going on some distance like this, night fell;
seeing a tree by the road, he stayed there.

218He laments, his heart in great distress;
hearing it, wood and stone would split.

219The inhabitants of a nearby village heard it —
what became of them I cannot tell.

220Srinivasa stays awake through the night, weeping;
by the Lord's will sleep overcame him.

221Sanatana, Rupa and the others, supremely merciful,
appeared to Srinivasa as if in a dream.

222The supreme, wondrous beauty of all the Gosvamis —
seeing it, Srinivasa's heart filled with boundless joy.

223His body thrilled with horripilation, he is bathed in tears;
rolling on the ground, he fell at their feet.

224All placed their feet on Srinivasa's head,
embraced him and consoled him in many ways.

225Seeing again and again how thin Srinivasa had become,
they stroke his body with their holy hands, tears in their eyes.

226Then Sri Gosvami, looking into Srinivasa's face,
speaks sweet words, absorbed in love:

227"O my son Srinivasa, what is there to say?
Now is not the time for you to grieve.

228Sri Gopala Bhatta is non-different from us;
go to him and receive the holy mantra.

229Taking all the books we have written,
go without delay to Gauda and spread them."

230Thus [it is said] in the Nava-padya:24
"In a dream Sri Rupa and the others, together with Srila Sanatana, said to you:
'This is no time for you to grieve. There is Gopala Bhatta —
therefore receive from him the best of mantras; and all the books written by us
take, go to Gauda, spread [our] teaching abundantly and instruct the Vaishnavas.'"

231Saying much in this way and showing mercy to Srinivasa,
they disappeared, remembering Gauranga.

232Srinivasa, having drunk the nectar of that vision and those words,
was overwhelmed, and in the morning he turned back [towards Vrindavana].

232aAnd again — what a wonder! Even before he entered Vrindavana,
the two Gosanis had gone [to Jiva and Gopala Bhatta].25

233Sri Rupa and Sri Sanatana, the two together,
that night speak to Sri Jiva as if in a dream:

234"On this twentieth day of the month of Vaishakha
the wondrous meeting we spoke of before will take place.

235Today he will come and enter Vrindavana;
meeting him, you will obtain supreme bliss.

236In the evening, at the arati of Sri Govinda-deva,
when the crowd has thinned, look for him.

237His complexion is like a golden champaka, his body is thin;
he is young, and tears flow ceaselessly from his eyes.

238He came from Gauda in great sorrow
and here heard of our disappearance.

239He firmly resolved to give up his body;
we appeared to him and consoled him in many ways.

240One cannot express how distressed his heart is;
as soon as you see him, you will know who he is.

241Have him take initiation from Sri Gopala Bhatta;
and when he has studied [our books], entrust all the books to him.

242Send him quickly to Gauda-mandala:
he will distribute the jewels of these books to the people.

243What more shall we say? Through Srinivasa
Prabhu Gaura-raya will accomplish many tasks."

244Having said much in this way to Sri Jiva,
they went to Sri Gopala Bhatta Gosvami and say,

245"Your Srinivasa has come from Gauda;
he has suffered much sorrow, more than can be told.

246Make him your disciple and comfort his heart."
Saying much in this way, they disappeared.

247Receiving such a command at dawn,
he rises and weeps, crying, "Rupa! Sanatana!"

248At that moment Sri Jiva arrived;
seeing him, [Gopala Bhatta] regained some composure.

249Sri Jiva bows down, bathed in tears;
Sri Bhatta Gosvami took Sri Jiva in his arms

250and bathed his body with tears;
his heart is bursting, he cannot restrain himself.

251As they told each other the commands received in the dream —
the state they were in I cannot describe.

252After a while Sri Bhatta Gosvami, composing himself,
calmed Sri Jiva with many words.

253The festival of Radha-ramana's ascending the throne was at hand;26
therefore he was busily making preparations.

254Sri Jiva, bowing again to the Bhatta Gosvami,
hurried to his own hut.

255His eagerness to see Srinivasa grew very great;
he told everyone that Srinivasa was coming.

256"When will he come?" — so he thinks,
and again and again he goes to look down the road.

257Meanwhile Srinivasa, in great agitation,
having entered Vrindavana, beholds its beauty.

258Over clusters of many flowers bees sweetly hum;
here and there peacocks and peahens dance.

259Cuckoos and other birds sing as if pouring nectar;
deer and other animals roam on all sides.

260The lovely [forest] is entwined with many trees and creepers;
seeing all this, he sheds tears ceaselessly.

261He saw the dwellings of the Vaishnavas of Vraja
and went to the temple of Sri Govinda-deva.

262Having darshan of Govinda in the evening,
his heart swelled with joy and he was bathed in tears.

263Absorbed in love, he fell to the ground and rolled about;
by the Lord's will he remained off to one side.

264At the evening arati there is a huge crowd;
Sri Jiva Gosvami is searching for Srinivasa.

265Srinivasa is lying off to one side;
[Jiva] suddenly came to that very spot.

266Seeing the transformations of bhava, Sri Jiva Gosani
knew this was Srinivasa and stood there.

267After a while [Srinivasa] mastered his bhava;
Sri Jiva himself lifted him from the ground.

268Srinivasa, drenched in his own tears,
falls at the feet of Sri Jiva Gosani, bowing down.

269Sri Jiva, deeply moved, speaks affectionate words;
stretching out both arms, he embraced Srinivasa.

270Embracing him tightly, he calls him "friend":
without asking, he knew who he was.

271The joy that arose at their meeting
I cannot describe here in detail.

272Sri Krishna Pandita, an associate of Sri Chaitanya,
seeing Srinivasa, rejoiced at heart.

273His virtues cannot be told with one mouth;
at that time he was the adhikari [chief servant] of Govinda.27

274Feeding Srinivasa with Sri mahaprasada,
he lovingly gave him prasada — betel and a garland.

275Who can describe how much affection he showed?
The news of Srinivasa's arrival spread everywhere.

276Sri Jiva Gosvami, taking his dear Srinivasa,
went to his own residence in great joy.

277There Radha-Damodara had already been laid to rest,
so there was no darshan that night.

278Sri Jiva gave Srinivasa lodging in a secluded place,
and Srinivasa stays there with a joyful heart.

279The night of the Vaishakha full moon — a marvellous beauty;
many flowers had blossomed, spreading their fragrance.

280He gazes at the sweetness of the many trees and creepers;
no sleep came to his eyes, and dawn arrived.

281In the morning, having finished his morning duties, bathing and so on,
he went and bowed at the feet of Sri Jiva Gosvami.

282Sri Jiva Gosvami treated him like a friend
and gave him darshan of Radha-Damodara.

283Joy wells up in Srinivasa's heart;
again and again he bows down, falling to the ground.

284A wondrous, incomparable, enchanting Deity;
as he gazes on Him, tears stream ceaselessly.

285For a while he gazed his fill:
Radha-Damodara is the treasure of Sri Jiva's life.

286By a command received in a dream, Sri Rupa with his own hands
made Sri Radha-Damodara and gave Him to Sri Jiva.28

287I am unable to describe Sri Jiva's deeds:
the lotus feet of Sri Rupa are his all in all.

288All this, in various languages and in Sanskrit,
was described by former poets renowned in the world.

289Thus in the Sadhana-dipika:29
"I ever bow to Sri Jiva, the resident of Vraja,
devoted to the two lotus feet of Sri Rupa, who gives bliss even to the dull."

290"The Deity Radha-Damodara, installed by Sri Rupa,
was given to Jiva Gosvami by Sri Rupa, the ocean of mercy."

291I have told briefly of His appearance:
Radha-Damodara is Jiva's very life.

292Sri Jiva is always in supreme joy,
beholding the pastimes of Sri Radha-Damodara.

293From time to time [the Lord] asks Sri Jiva for food,
and Sri Jiva sees how the Lord eats.

294One day, smiling, He plays the flute
and says to Sri Jiva, "Look at Me!"

295The age of kishora, a world-enchanting appearance —
the moment he saw Him, Sri Jiva fell unconscious.

296Regaining consciousness, his heart swelled with bliss,
and tears flowed from both his long eyes.

297I have told a little in passing — there are many such events:
Radha-Damodara attracts every heart.

298Sri Jiva Gosvami showed mercy to Srinivasa
and entrusted him to the feet of Radha-Damodara.

299The samadhi of Sri Rupa Gosvami is right there;
[Jiva] himself took Srinivasa to it.

300Srinivasa, beholding the holy samadhi,
is bathed in tears and falls prostrate.

301Sri Jiva, consoling Srinivasa, quickly took him
to Sri Gopala Bhatta Gosvami.

302Sri Bhatta Gosvami is sitting in seclusion;
tears stream ceaselessly from both his eyes.

303Srinivasa, looking at Sri Bhatta Gosvami,
lost all composure and rolls on the ground.

304Again and again he bows down, tears flowing from his eyes;
Sri Jiva introduced Srinivasa.

305Although the Bhatta was burning in the fire of separation,
still he rejoiced at seeing Srinivasa.

306Affectionately placing his feet on Srinivasa's head,
he told him to sit, speaking kind words.

307Then he asked Srinivasa for his news,
and Srinivasa told him everything from beginning to end.

308Hearing this, the Gosvami, deeply distressed at heart,
says again and again how grieved he is.

309Then he praised Srinivasa's good fortune
and told of the command of Sanatana and Rupa in the dream.

310Sri Jiva Gosvami, having heard the Gosvami,
seizing the moment, speaks sweet words:

311"Srinivasa longs with all his heart for initiation."
The Gosvami consented — for the second lunar day.30

312Sri Jiva Gosvami, with great joy,
showed Sri Radha-ramana to Srinivasa.

313The Deity of Sri Radha-ramana is supremely enchanting;
only the fortunate are granted to see Him.

314His sweetest grace is known throughout the world;
when He appeared, there was great rejoicing in Vrindavana.

315Listen, I shall tell a little of His appearance:
Sri Radha-ramana is [the Deity] known to the Bhatta Gosvami.

316Sri Gauranga-deva gave the Gosvami a command:
"You will see Hari from a shalagrama."31

317By Gauranga's command the Bhatta reveals this to Sri Rupa,
and then Rupa Gosvami says in loving rapture:

318"Sri Govinda-deva is your all in all,
and yet it is His desire that you serve Him separately."

319And then, after some days, from the shalagrama
He Himself appeared, for all people to see.

320Who can understand the Gosvami's intention?
What a wondrous form appeared, conquering the world!

321Sri Govinda, Gopinatha, Madana-mohana —
in that order: the face, the chest and the holy feet of these three.32

322The darshan of the three Lords together in one place —
the Gosani had conceived such a design beforehand.

323Sanatana Gosvami, Bhugarbha and all the others
rejoiced to see the service of Sri Radha-ramana.

324In the month of Vaishakha, at the auspicious time of the full moon,
Sri Radha-ramana ascended the throne.

325At His ascending the throne there was a great festival;
the Lord who is subdued by the Bhatta's love is famous throughout the world.

326Thus beautiful Radha-ramana appeared;
the wise have described it in Bengali and in Sanskrit.

327Thus in the Sadhana-dipika:33
"I bow to Gopala Bhatta, for whom the feet of Govinda are everything,
who by Sri Rupa's command manifested a separate service.

328Sri Radha-ramana-deva is held to be [the Lord] of his service;
He is the One whom the skilful Srila Rupa beheld in meditation.
The reason for the command I heard there from the mouths of reliable persons."

329And there, as is well known:
"I bow to Sri Gopala Bhatta, the resident of Vraja,
the nephew of Sri Prabodhananda, an abode of mercy."

330Thus in the Madana-raga-valli of Sri Manohara Raya, a disciple in the branch of Sri Srinivasa Acharya Thakura:34
Sri Madana-gopala with Sri Radhika,
Sri Govinda-lala with the Queen of Vrindavana,

331Sri Gopinatha with the Daughter of Vrishabhanu —
seeing and serving Them, he deemed his life fulfilled.

332But his longing to serve [a Deity] himself grew;
it is clear that the Lord wished [to appear] through the Gosani.

333One day, thinking only of a [visible] form,
he pondered in his mind the longing of his heart.

334Knowing the desire of Sri Gopala Bhatta Gosani,
[the Lord] Himself manifested His form for Sri Gopala.

335With his companions he held a festival and performed the abhisheka;
thus the service of Sri Radha-ramana became manifest.

336Building a temple, he established his service;
it is most wondrous — however much one tells, it is never all told.

337Thus I have told briefly of Radha-ramana's appearance,
in which lies the dawning of every joy.

338Radha-ramana is the life of Bhatta Gopala;
apart from Him there is nothing else, waking or dreaming.

339With his whole being he drinks the beauty of Sri Radha-ramana;
Sri Gopala Bhatta is Guna- [or] Ananga-manjari.

340Thus in the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (184):35
"She who was Ananga-manjari is now Gopala Bhatta;
some, however, call the Bhatta Gosvami Sri Guna-manjari."

341Intoxicated with Radha-ramana's beauty and qualities,
he dresses Him in various flower garments, having received permission.

342In his service supreme bliss increases at every moment;
he constantly remembers his service to Sri Gaurachandra.

343In his own home, at his father's command, he had served Gaurachand;36
remembering it, he cannot keep his composure.

344Overwhelmed, he is bathed in tears
and looks again and again at Sri Radha-ramana.

345Sri Radha-ramana, subdued by Gopala's love,
at that very moment took the form of Sri Gaurasundara.

346Youthful age, attire that maddens the world;
at the splendour of His beauty millions of Madanas swoon.

347Beholding this beauty, his heart overflowed with bliss;
crying, "What have I seen!" he falls to the ground.

348Abundant horripilation, his eyes swimming in tears,
he sings the virtues of Sri Radha-ramana — Gorachand.

349Whatever desire arises in Sri Gopala Bhatta's heart,
Sri Radha-ramana fulfils it that very moment.

350Known to the world is this incomparable relationship:
Sri Radha-ramana is the Lord of Gopala's life.

351Having darshan of such a Radha-ramana,
Srinivasa fell to the ground, bowing down.

352He is bathed in tears and cannot be calm;
so many words from the depths of his heart rise within him!

353Surrendering himself to Sri Radha-ramana,
he gazed on Him for a while, holding himself steady.

354Sri Jiva Gosvami, taking his dear Srinivasa
and bowing to Sri Radha-ramana, went

355to Lokanatha and Bhugarbha Gosvami
and told them of Srinivasa's coming.37

356Though the hearts of both were in great distress,
hearing that Srinivasa had come, they rejoiced.

357Srinivasa bowed at the feet of both,
and both embraced him with great tenderness.

358In loving rapture they could not let him out of their arms
and bathed Srinivasa in tears.

359They entrusted him to the lotus feet of Sri Radha-vinoda;
both showed Srinivasa great mercy.

360What was Srinivasa's loving rapture
at the darshan of Sri Radha-vinoda — who will describe it?

361Then Sri Jiva, taking Srinivasa,
went for the darshan of Gopinatha.

362Srinivasa, at the darshan of Sri Gopinatha,
lost his composure; streams flowed from both his eyes.

363There Sri Paramananda and Sri Madhu Pandita —
all rejoiced on seeing Srinivasa.38

364The affection they showed cannot be described.
From there he went and saw Madana-mohana.

365Srinivasa, beholding Madana-mohana,
cannot keep his composure: his heart overflows with love.

366Again and again he bows to Madana-gopala;
tears run down his face and chest.

367After a while Srinivasa grew calm;
Sri Jiva Gosvami introduced him to everyone.

368Krishnadasa Brahmachari and all the others,39
in loving rapture, embraced him tightly.

369Srinivasa bowed at everyone's feet,
and all showed Srinivasa great mercy.

370For the darshan of the samadhi of Sanatana Gosvami
everyone took Srinivasa.

371Seeing the samadhi of Sanatana Gosvami,
Srinivasa fell and rolled on the ground.

372What became of Srinivasa cannot be described;
at Srinivasa's weeping everyone weeps.

373All, with great tenderness for Srinivasa,
consoled him with sweet words.

374Sri Jiva Gosvami, taking Srinivasa,
came to his own residence in great joy.

375"Tomorrow morning Sri Gosani will make Srinivasa his disciple,"
he announced everywhere.

376Srinivasa praised his own good fortune
and spent that day in various discussions.

377The next day, having bathed, Srinivasa
went with Sri Jiva to the Gosvami.

378There the Bhatta Gosvami, full of supreme love,
was performing the service of Radha-ramana.

Notes

  1. Vamshivadana (Vamshi-vadana Thakura) — an associate of the Lord who, after Mahaprabhu's sannyasa, served Vishnupriya in Navadvipa.
  2. Vishnupriya — the consort of Sri Chaitanya; Narahari calls her Ishvari ("the Mistress").
  3. As befits a chaste lady, Vishnupriya does not show herself to Srinivasa but speaks while remaining concealed.
  4. After each round of names Vishnupriya set aside one grain of rice; the rice of these grains she cooked and offered to the Lord, eating only a little of it.
  5. Advaita had already disappeared by this time (BR 3.330); here He appears to Srinivasa.
  6. Madana-gopala — the Deity of Advaita Acharya at Shantipura.
  7. Parameshvari (Parameshvara) Dasa — one of the twelve gopalas, an associate of Nityananda (CC Adi 11).
  8. Vasudha and Jahnava are the consorts of Nityananda; Virabhadra (Virachandra) is His son.
  9. Virloka — so in the editions; apparently a locality near Khanakula (the 1960 edition puts the word in quotation marks as a name).
  10. Khanakula-Krishnanagara on the Dvarakeshvara river — the seat of Abhirama Thakura and his Deity Gopinatha.
  11. Abhirama Thakura (Rama Dasa) — one of the twelve gopalas; in Krishna's pastimes the cowherd boy Shridama (GGD).
  12. A kard (kara) is a counting unit of small cowrie shells: Abhirama gave him a trifling sum.
  13. The Darukeshvara (Dvarakeshvara) is the river on which Khanakula stands.
  14. Abhirama's whip Jayamangala: according to tradition, whoever Abhirama touches with it obtains prema (cf. PV).
  15. Agrahayana (Margashirsha) — November–December.
  16. Agradvipa — a village on the Ganges, the place of Govinda Ghosha; Kantaka-nagara is Katwa, where the Lord accepted sannyasa (CB Madhya 28; CC Adi 17).
  17. Maudeshvara — a Shiva temple in Birbhum, on the road to Ekachakra.
  18. Kundali-damana ("the subduing of the serpent") — the place where, according to local tradition, Nityananda subdued a serpent.
  19. Ekachakra (Birbhum) — the birthplace of Nityananda; Hadai Ojha (Hadai Pandita) is His father.
  20. At Gaya the Lord met Ishvara Puri and received initiation from him (CB Adi 17; CC Adi 17).
  21. Chandrashekhara — a vaidya (according to the CC, a scribe) of Kashi in whose house the Lord stayed (CC Madhya 17, 20, 25). Only Narahari mentions his disciple.
  22. Vishrama-ghata — the principal ghat on the Yamuna at Mathura, where, according to tradition, Krishna rested after killing Kamsa.
  23. In Narahari's account Srinivasa reaches Vraja after Sanatana and Rupa have already disappeared; Kashishvara and Raghunatha Bhatta have also departed.
  24. The Nava-padya — a collection of verses by Nrisimha Kaviraja, a disciple of Srinivasa (cf. 3.78).
  25. Couplet 232a is absent in the 1960 edition; it is present in the editions of 1888 and 1912/13.
  26. Gopala Bhatta's Deity Radha-ramana appeared from a shalagrama on the Vaishakha full moon (below, 4.316–326); the anniversary of that appearance is meant here.
  27. Krishna Pandita — according to Narahari, an associate of the Lord and at that time the chief servant (adhikari) of the Govinda temple in Vrindavana.
  28. Radha-Damodara — the Deity of Jiva Gosvami in Vrindavana.
  29. The Sadhana-dipika of Radha-Krishna Gosvami (cf. BR 2.473–483).
  30. That is, on the second lunar day after the Vaishakha full moon.
  31. According to tradition, the Lord told Gopala Bhatta to serve shalagramas and promised to appear to him from a shalagrama.
  32. Traditionally it is said that Radha-ramana has the face of Govinda, the chest of Gopinatha and the feet of Madana-mohana.
  33. The Sadhana-dipika of Radha-Krishna Gosvami.
  34. Manohara Raya (Manohara Dasa) — a disciple in the line of Srinivasa Acharya; the Madana-raga-valli is a Bengali work.
  35. The verse number is given in the 1912/13 edition. According to the GGD, Gopala Bhatta is Ananga-manjari (Radha's younger sister), and in the opinion of some, Guna-manjari.
  36. On young Gopala's service to the Lord in the house of his father Venkata Bhatta at Srirangam, see BR 1.
  37. Lokanatha Gosvami and Bhugarbha Gosvami; Radha-vinoda is Lokanatha's Deity.
  38. Paramananda Bhattacharya and Madhu Pandita — the servants of Gopinatha (BR 2.473–483).
  39. Krishnadasa Brahmachari — the servant of Madana-mohana.
